supersededScheduleReview.conclusion: The 72 placements pass formal prerequisite/offering and numerical checks; withdrawal is a programme-level academic decision, not a schedule failure. No UCR schedule is retained in the final exception.

academicReview.judgment: A coherent UCR programme in law, economics and public finance can be built, with genuine legal and taxation-policy contributions. It does not sustain the fiscal-legal inquiry that defines this target: interpreting tax legislation and applying it to income, profits, VAT, tax procedure and international taxing rights. Those topics organise Erasmus’s progression, skills and research, rather than merely a professional credential. The broad supporting subjects and a public-economics course therefore do not establish a sufficiently close target-level response under the current course evidence.
academicReview.strongestPlausibleAlternative: The strongest positive argument is substantial: the closest 24-course programme contains 60 EC of real legal foundations/branches, 37.5 EC of economics including Public Economics, accounting, finance, research and rhetoric. It can implement a coherent law-and-public-finance education and genuinely addresses the societal/economic question in row 893. The failure is more specific than missing a degree label or professional qualification: the only explicit UCR taxation teaching is economic public-policy analysis, while the legal courses do not document fiscal legal interpretation, assessment/collection procedures, taxable income/profits, VAT or allocation of taxing rights. Their combination does not establish a sustained inquiry into taxation as a legal institution. Assigning fiscal projects, relabelling general EU/private law or relying on optional research would invent that missing organising link.

externalReview.findings: The current 2026–2027 Fiscaal recht OER, linked by the official ESL regulations page, controls. Articles 6, 10 and 11 and the visible PDF page 4 establish 25 unique components: 60 EC in each of three years, 180 EC overall. All previous component identities and credit weights are retained after checking the current edition. The 2026 first-year skills code is RR/RD125; obsolete RR/RD122 transitional provisions do not create an additional component. Article 4 permits full-time and part-time registration; this normalized target is full-time, Dutch-taught with the named international/EU-law assessment in English under article 5. There is no formal bachelor route to select; the generic 15-EC minor is retained under article 13, not populated for UCR convenience. A non-EUR minor requires an internally coherent package, Examination Board approval and an application eight weeks before study. Article 15 requires the skills-I evidence portfolio, completed tasks and attendance at prescribed meetings; article 16 requires all skills-II assessments and a passed Moot Court. Article 17 places research skills and the bachelor thesis within the 10-EC skills-III component, weighted 30% and 70%; the thesis requires at least 6 and the whole trajectory is mandatory. Articles 27 and 38 require the applicable first-year BSA before second-year exams. Appendix 4 requires completed B1 and at least 42 B2 EC for B3, with minor access from the third registration year even without the latter threshold. The limited 28-EC provisional skills-III entry is conditional on subsequently meeting 42 EC; it is not the normal pathway. The retained sequential 60+60+60 pathway satisfies the ordinary conditions. Old 45-EC rules in historical appendices do not control a 2026 entrant. Current public course descriptions corroborate academic content but their generic criminal-law progression and separately headed thesis are not added as extra Fiscaal recht requirements. No future course timetable or professional/master admission is guaranteed.
